title: AKS Overview for Developers
description: Get an introduction to Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) and understand its core components from a developer's perspective.

data.text: Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) is a managed Kubernetes service on Azure. It handles the control plane (master nodes) while you manage the worker nodes (agent nodes) where your containers run.
As a developer, you interact with AKS mainly through YAML manifests and kubectl commands to deploy and manage your applications.

items: Pod: The smallest deployable unit - runs one or more containers
Deployment: Manages a set of identical Pods and handles updates
Service: Exposes Pods via a stable network endpoint
Ingress: Routes external HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Services
Secret: Stores sensitive data like passwords and keys
Namespace: Virtual cluster for resource isolation

data.title: YAML - Simple Kubernetes Deployment
data.content:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: myapp-deployment
  labels:
    app: myapp
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: myapp
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: myapp
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: myapp
        image: myregistry.azurecr.io/myapp:1.0
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080

data.title: Control Plane vs Node Pool
data.text: AKS manages the control plane (API server, etcd, scheduler) for free. You only pay for the agent nodes in the node pools. Azure also provides free control plane upgrades and patches.

terms.definition: Azure Kubernetes Service - a managed Kubernetes offering where Azure manages the control plane.
The smallest deployable Kubernetes unit, containing one or more containers that share storage and networking.
A Kubernetes resource that manages Pod replicas and handles rolling updates.
A group of VMs (agent nodes) that run Pods in an AKS cluster.

data.caption: AKS cluster architecture overview
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    subgraph CP[Control Plane - Managed by Azure]
        API[API Server]
        ETCD[etcd]
        SCHED[Scheduler]
    end
    subgraph NP1[Node Pool 1: Linux]
        N1[Node 1] --> P1[Pod A]
        N1 --> P2[Pod B]
        N2[Node 2] --> P3[Pod C]
    end
    subgraph NP2[Node Pool 2: Windows]
        N3[Node 3] --> P4[Pod D]
    end
    API --> NP1
    API --> NP2

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: AKS is a managed Kubernetes service on Azure
Azure manages the control plane; you manage node pools
Pods are the smallest deployable units
Deployments manage Pod replicas and updates
data.takeaway: AKS gives you full Kubernetes power with managed control plane operations.
